claims.text: The reported TiVNbTa baseline has a single-phase dendritic BCC microstructure.
The room-temperature yield strength of the TiVNbTa baseline is approximately 800 MPa.
At 1273 K, the TiVNbTa baseline has yield and compressive strengths of approximately 330 MPa and 423 MPa, respectively.
The proposed intervention is to substitute approximately 5–10 at.% of a TiVNbTa component with W to form a quinary TiVNbTaW alloy.
The modified alloy is intended to retain a single-phase BCC structure.
Adding W will increase the high-temperature yield strength of TiVNbTa by approximately 20–50% at 1273 K.
Adding W will enhance the thermal stability of TiVNbTa.
The W-modified alloy will be more suitable as an intermediate heat-transfer layer between W and CuCrZr.
The strength and stability improvements will occur without a severe loss of ductility.
Arc melting followed by homogenization will ensure phase uniformity.
The intervention will maintain a refined, single-phase BCC microstructure.
W addition will increase lattice distortion in TiVNbTa.
W addition may produce finer grains in TiVNbTa.
The refined, distorted BCC structure will favor edge-dislocation-controlled deformation at high temperature.
W has a higher melting point than the constituents relevant to the proposed alloy modification.
W provides strong solid-solution strengthening in TiVNbTa.
W addition increases the energy barrier for thermally activated dislocation glide.
Increasing the glide barrier promotes edge-dislocation mobility.
W addition will improve the thermal conductivity of TiVNbTa.
The modified alloy will avoid formation of brittle secondary phases at the proposed W content.

contradictions.description: The mechanism says W raises the energy barrier for dislocation glide while simultaneously claiming that this promotes dislocation mobility; a higher glide barrier ordinarily implies reduced mobility unless an additional distinction or mechanism is supplied.

The intervention specifies substituting W for an unspecified existing component, whereas the experiment describes adding 5–10 at.% W. These routes imply different final compositions and are not compositionally equivalent without further definition.
